transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in, I really appreciate it. I hope I'm not taking up time from someone who needs it more, but... I've just been having a bit of a hard time lately. 

Um, it's actually a little embarrassing to admit, but... we've been getting some foreclosure notices in the mail. And ever since they started coming, I just... I feel like I’m coming apart at the seams, if that makes sense? I've been, well, sitting out in my truck crying before my shift starts, which is just so silly and unprofessional of me. And I jump every single time my phone rings. 

I work as a heavy equipment mechanic, and I've even been snapping at the apprentices, which isn't fair to them at all. I'm just so distracted that I'm making these really stupid mistakes in the repair bay—things I never, ever would’ve made before. I just want to get back to being reliable and doing a good job again. Is that... does that sound like an okay reason to be here?
Have you noticed that things you usually enjoy, like hobbies or spending time with family, don’t bring you the same amount of pleasure or interest lately?

Um, well... I guess I haven't really noticed a huge change there? I mean, I still love my family, of course. I'm so lucky to have them. And I still try to keep up with my usual stuff on the weekends when I can. 

I might be a little more tired than usual, maybe? So sometimes I just want to rest instead of going out. But I don't think I've lost interest in things completely. I'm still trying my best to stay positive and be involved. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your question right.

Do you find yourself worrying a lot about different things in your life, even when there isn’t an immediate problem, or does your anxiety mostly come up in specific situations like when you get a notice in the mail or your phone rings?

Um, well... I don't think I'm a worrier in general. I really try hard not to be one of those people who stresses over every little thing, you know? I always try to be strong for my family. 

So, no, I don't really sit around worrying if there isn't a problem. It really is just... just the house stuff. Like you said, it hits me when I check the mail, or when an unknown number pops up on my phone and I think it's the bank calling again. If it weren't for those notices, I think I'd be completely fine. I'm usually a very steady person, I promise. It's just this one big thing that's making me act so out of character. 

Is that... is that helpful? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of answers.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep, energy level, or appetite since this situation with the foreclosure notices started?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I think I'm doing okay with all of that. I definitely still eat dinner with my family every night—I really wouldn't want them to start worrying about me, you know? 

And my sleep is... well, it's mostly fine. I might toss and turn just a tiny bit if I'm thinking about the bank, but I always make sure I get enough rest so I can get up for my shift. I know I mentioned being a little tired earlier, but my energy is generally okay. I'm really trying hard to keep my routine normal and not let this affect my health. I need to stay strong for everyone. 

Does... does that make sense? Is it a good sign that those things are still pretty normal? I hope that's what you were asking.
Have you felt down, hopeless, or like you’re not worth much, even when you’re not thinking about the foreclosure situation?

Um... no, definitely not. I really try to be a positive person, you know? I don't feel hopeless or... or worthless at all. 

I work really hard at the shop—being a heavy equipment mechanic, you kind of just have to figure out how to fix what's broken and keep moving forward. I try to apply that to my life, too. So if I ever do feel a little low, it's strictly just because of the letters from the bank. When my mind is off the house situation, I feel completely normal and capable. 

I really don't want you to think I'm just sitting around feeling sorry for myself, because I promise I'm not. I'm trying so hard to keep a good attitude and just push through this. Is that... is that the right way to handle it? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how I'm doing.

latest_inference.note: The patient's symptoms are primarily related to stressors associated with the foreclosure notices, without evidence of major depression or generalized anxiety. This supports a diagnosis of adjustment disorder with anxiety and depressed mood (F43.22) as the symptoms are time-limited and situational.

inference_history.note: The patient presented symptoms of emotional distress, crying episodes, anxiety (e.g., jumping at phone ringing), irritability, difficulty concentrating, and functional impairment at work in the context of a psychosocial stressor (foreclosure notices). This leads to consideration of adjustment disorder with mixed anxiety and depressed mood (F43.22), moderate depressive episode (F32.1), generalized anxiety disorder (F41.1), and unspecified nonorganic mental disorder (F54).

The patient has not endorsed a loss of interest or pleasure in activities, which reduces the likelihood of F54 (Personality disorder, unspecified) being relevant. The primary symptoms still align with adjustment disorder, major depressive episode, and generalized anxiety disorder.
